title: Reformed reject Rome’s intrinsic venials—yet allow a commodious use of the names
source_text: XXIV. Porro ex iis quae dicta sunt apparet Reformatos non probare distinctionem peccati in mortale & veniale, prout in Schola Romana communiter exponitur. Cum enim existiment omne peccatum per se, & natura sua poenam & mortem aeternam mereri, concedere non possunt peccata quaedam esse per se non mortalia, sed venialia. Attamen distinctionem istam non prorsus rejiciunt, sed commodo sensu illam usurpari posse fatentur.
pass_a_gloss: Further from what has been said it appears that the Reformed do not approve the distinction of sin into mortal and venial as it is commonly set forth in the Roman School. For since they judge that every sin of itself and by its nature merits eternal penalty and death, they cannot grant that certain sins are of themselves not mortal but venial. Yet they do not wholly reject that distinction, but confess that it can be used in a commodious sense.
pass_b_english: Reformed deny Rome’s claim that some sins are by nature non-mortal.
They still allow mortal/venial labels when taken in a careful, commodious sense.
